messages.subject: NAs after protein group comparison
messages.body_plain:
Dear MSstats developer team,
I have to do a power analysis on a pilot study in order to plan the real study.
It is DIA data analyzed in DIA-NN and I manually brought the data in 10 column format.

When I run the proteingroupcomparison I only get NAs for FCs pVals etc.

After dataprocess, the Abundance values were calculated, so I am not sure where the problem lies.

I had the same problem before and Mateusz found that my annotation was wrong, so here I already checked the annotation twice for double annotated bioreplicates and even changed the bioreplicates in the data to make sure, there is no problem with the assignment of
Condition <-> BioReplicate

I set up a really small reproducible sample, which I will attach.

Best, Klemens

messages.subject: Re: NAs after protein group comparison
messages.body_plain:
I cannot attach the R script. Here is the script for the example:

#packages
library(MSstats)

#set working directory to current folder of R script
setwd(dirname(rstudioapi::getActiveDocumentContext()$path))

# input
test2 <-  readRDS(file = "test.rds")

##### msstats analysis ######
msstats_dataprocess <- MSstats::dataProcess(raw = test2,
  normalization = F,
  MBimpute = F)

#investigate this
msstats_dataprocess$ProcessedData %>% View()

#contrast.matrix for comparison
comparison <-  data.frame(V1 = 1, V2 = -1)
colnames(comparison) <- levels(msstats_dataprocess$ProcessedData$GROUP_ORIGINAL)
rownames(comparison) <- c("Group.A vs Group.B")

msstats_comparison <- MSstats::groupComparison(data = msstats_dataprocess, contrast.matrix = comparison)

msstats_comparison$ComparisonResult %>% View()

> > > > > > > > > > > > > Hi,
> > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > the dataProcess function does several things and at each step there's something you can do to improve the running time. I'll assume there's no fractionation in your data (if there is, only some details change):
> > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > >  - dataProcess requires that there is a row for each feature in each run. If your input data satisfy this requirement, there will be no need for potentially lengthy computations,
> > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > - then, dataProcess performs normalization. If you can normalize data in an efficient way outside of dataProcess, it should speed it up significantly (just set normalization = "NONE"),
> > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > - selecting features for summarization via "highQuality" method can take some time - if you want speed, choose "topN" with a low N (3 is the default for this method, but by default dataProcess uses all features),
> > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > - another operation is finding values that will be considered as censored. You can set maxQuantileforCensored = NULL to skip this (and perhaps do it outside of dataProcess function),
> > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > - with data in the right format (normalized, with a row for every run and feature etc), you can run dataProcess for each protein separately or for batches of proteins and parallelize your code.
> > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > Btw we will be releasing a new version of MSstats in October. The new version will be easier to work with for big datasets

> > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > Kind regards,

Claire

Hi Claire,

I shortly review it. Here are some solutions for your case.
- Run column should be the same as Raw.file.
- if you have technical replicates, please add 'TechReplicate' column in annotation. I guess the current 'Run' column has tech replicate information. please replace the column name 'Run' to 'TechReplicate'

Hope that it works.

- Meena

messages.subject: confusion about MBimpute behavior and possible bug
messages.subject_clean: confusion about MBimpute behavior and possible bug
messages.body_plain:
What is the intended behavior of dataProcess when MBimpute = FALSE and censoredInt="NA"?  According to help(dataProcess), and confirmed by the message linked below from Meena in 2016, I expect imputation to happen but using the minimum value per feature instead of model-based.  With the current version of MSstats, it appears that imputation does not happen (confirmed by column NumImputedFeature in  output$RunLevelData, and also patterns in the protein intensity data).

https://groups.google.com/g/msstats/c/QzNVnF2ASXc/m/Vs9F_pjjCAAJ

Is this a bug or expected behavior?  If it's expected behavior, then the help docs should be clarified.  If it's a bug and you decide to fix it, then the help docs should probably also be clarified with instructions on how to turn off all imputation because many people think MBimpute=FALSE is sufficient, and they may suddenly have imputation turned on when they don't expect it.

In the code, this turning off of all imputation seems to happen because an if statement compares zero against the sum of a cen data column (0,1 for censored or not) that doesn't exist so is NULL.  sum(NULL) evaluates to zero, so it acts like there are no censored values, which I don't think was expected. (See line 2406 in current DataProcess.R)  It looks like the code that made that column was moved inside a block that only evaluates when MBimpute=TRUE some time in the last five years.  See attached screen shot from a github diff of dataProcess.

Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: Imputation with MBimpute
messages.body_plain:
Corrected answer. This logic was changed since v3.5.5.

MBimpute=TRUE : imputation, with model-based value
MBimpute=FALSE : no imputation

- Meena

On Thursday, June 23, 2016 at 9:14:15 AM UTC-7 mnch...@gmail.com wrote:
> Thank you for giving us to clarify the combination of options.
>
> 1. imputation, with model-based value
> quant <- dataProcess(msstats.raw, fillIncompleteRows=TRUE, normalization="quantile")
>
>
> 2. imputation, not model based imputation, but just impute with minimum value per feature for NA censored value.
> quant <- dataProcess(msstats.raw, fillIncompleteRows=TRUE, normalization="quantile", MBimpute=FALSE)
>
>
> 3. no imputation, there is no censored Intensity.
> quant <- dataProcess(msstats.raw, fillIncompleteRows=TRUE, normalization="quantile", censoredInt=NULL)
>
> all three combination will have different results.
> If you don't want any imputation, please use option 3.
>
> Hope to help.
>
> -Meena
